anna_ml: Quick summary from today's KV-cache quant experiments on Llama-2-13B (hf weights) — compared FP8-KV vs INT8-KV across streaming and batch profiles. TL;DR: FP8-KV saves ~22% GPU memory vs INT8-KV on 8k contexts but increases P99 by ~5ms for streaming single-token steps; INT8-KV (AWQ+per-channel) has lower tail latency but slightly higher steady memory. Full numbers below and artifacts uploaded. :floppy_disk:

jake_infra: Nice. What runtime/build and hardware?

anna_ml: Tested on our dedicated cluster (A10G and A100 80GB). Runtime: rwl-infer v2.7 with continuous-batching disabled for the streaming runs, enabled for batch. Gym commands: 
```
./run_bakeoff --model l2-13b --context 8192 --batch 1 --kv-quant fp8 --runtime rwl-2.7 --pins=host
./run_bakeoff --model l2-13b --context 8192 --batch 1 --kv-quant int8-awq --runtime rwl-2.7 --pins=host
```

ravi_research: Did you do warm vs cold-cache? KV quant often interacts with cold-start caching.

anna_ml: Yep. Two modes: cold (first request after model load) and warm (after streaming a prefix of 512 tokens so KV is populated). Observed that FP8-KV gives bigger wins on warm memory (because quantized KV compresses live cache) but cold P99 suffers a bit due to additional unpack/scale steps during first few decodings.

sandy_eng: numbers? put a tiny table pls.

anna_ml: Paste of the short table from the perf run (A100, single client streaming, 8k context):

```
Config             | Mem (GB) | P50(ms) | P95(ms) | P99(ms) | QoR delta (EM)
-------------------|----------|---------|---------|---------|---------------
FP8-KV (warm)      | 32.4     | 11.2    | 18.6    | 28.1    | -0.4%
INT8-KV (warm)     | 41.7     | 10.8    | 17.9    | 23.0    | -0.2%
FP8-KV (cold)      | 34.1     | 12.8    | 21.4    | 35.6    | -0.6%
INT8-KV (cold)     | 43.0     | 11.0    | 18.5    | 24.2    | -0.25%
```

anna_ml: Memory numbers are resident GPU after load + peak during generation. FP8 reduces resident KV footprint but adds small compute overhead for dequant/rescale on hot paths. QoR was measured on our 1k-sample QA eval suite (EM = exact match).

jake_infra: What about batching throughput (batch=8)? Any inverse effect?

anna_ml: For batch=8 (same context), INT8 had slightly better throughput (tokens/s) because AWQ path vectorizes better with our kernel selection. Quick throughput numbers (tokens/s): FP8-KV batch8 = 315 tps, INT8-KV batch8 = 338 tps. Latency P99 for batched requests became less differentiating because batching hides per-token overhead.

ravi_research: Did you compare GPTQ vs AWQ variants for INT8? Which performed better in KV case?

anna_ml: Tried GPTQ-llm + AWQ. AWQ-per-channel had the best memory/latency balance for KV because it preserves magnitude patterns per head. GPTQ sometimes needed per-layer tuning for KV matrices — gave slightly worse P99 and occasional token-level decoding diffs on long contexts. We flagged 12 samples failing at >32k context with GPTQ (repro script attached).

eval-bot: Perf artifacts uploaded: s3://redwood-artifacts/kv-quant/1719001234/ (logs, profiles, model diffs, eval-report.json) :white_check_mark:

sandy_eng: Any actionable guidance for Dedicated vs Private deployments?

anna_ml: For Dedicated (predictable GPUs) INT8-KV AWQ is a safe default if you want lower tail latency and slightly higher mem. For Private/on-prem where memory is constrained and customers prefer smaller deployment footprint, FP8-KV is attractive but add the following mitigations:
- enable per-request KV prefetching for cold-starts
- use warm-up prefix of ~512 tokens on model load for streaming apps
- tune kernel selection to prefer fused dequant/rescale kernels (we added a flag --prefer-fused-kernels)

jake_infra: Any stability issues or fragmentation?

anna_ml: One note: FP8 paths currently allocate temporary buffers more frequently which increased GPU memory fragmentation in our earlier driver; we mitigated by batching allocs and pinning KV slab memory. After that, fragmentation not observable in steady-state.

ravi_research: How about accuracy regression patterns? Are errors concentrated on numeric/float-sensitive tasks?

anna_ml: Mostly on arithmetic/formula-heavy QA and some long-context coreference. EM drops were small (<1%) but more pronounced for >16k contexts. We logged token-level diffs and will add a small prompt set to the regression alerting.

sandy_eng: Great. Can you add a short runbook for rollout flags? Ops wants small checklist.

anna_ml: Will push a short runbook to the repo tonight. Quick rollout notes here: 
1) start with INT8-KV on canary (5% traffic)
2) monitor P99 & QoR delta against baseline -> threshold: P99 increase < +3ms and QoR delta < 0.5%
3) if mem constrained, try FP8-KV on canary with warm-up prefix enabled
4) fallback: auto-route to FP16-KV if QoR regressions spike

jake_infra: Thanks — can you attach the exact run command for ops once you push the runbook?

anna_ml: Yup, will do. Uploading runbook + diff patch later today.

eval-bot: Regression alert seed set for FP8-KV: 1k prompt set, notify #eng-sre if EM drop > 0.7%

sandy_eng: Awesome, thanks team :tada:
